title: King's Indian Attack: the ideas
line: A calm setup behind the bishop on the long diagonal, then a pawn push toward the king.

steps.text: Bring the knight out first. It watches the center squares d4 and e5.

also.e2e4: That is the most played first move, the king pawn opening. This lesson starts with the knight.
also.d2d4: That is the queen pawn opening, also sound. This lesson starts with the knight.
also.c2c4: That is the English Opening, also sound. This lesson starts with the knight.

steps.after: Black takes the center with its queen pawn.

steps.text: Move the pawn on g2 one square to open the long diagonal.

also.c2c4: That is the Réti Opening, also sound. This lesson builds the King's Indian Attack.
also.d2d4: That is a queen pawn game, also sound. This lesson builds the King's Indian Attack.

steps.after: This is the King's Indian Attack.

steps.text: Put the bishop on the long diagonal. Your king will castle behind it.

also.c2c4: That turns it into a Réti Opening, also sound. This lesson keeps building the setup.

steps.text: Castle early. The king is safe behind the bishop.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It gets the king pawn push ready.
Bring the other knight out behind the pawns. It backs up the king pawn too.
Push the king pawn two squares. Now White has its share of the center.
Put a rook behind the king pawn. It backs up the next push.
steps.after: Black plays on the queenside, far from your attack.

steps.text: Push the king pawn on. It chases the knight on f6 away from Black's king.
steps.after: The pawn on e5 cramps Black's kingside. White's knights and queen head toward the king next.

summary: White sets up calmly behind the bishop on the long diagonal, then pushes the king pawn to attack the king.
